23 October 2026 · Rome · 8:30 p.m.

By invitation only · Venue to be announced

Professor Gabriele Pao-Pei Andreoli and the Institute for Advance Studies and Cooperation invite distinguished guests, friends and members of the World Changers community to a closing evening of celebration, artistic discovery and shared purpose.

Following the Vatican gathering, this reception will bring together participants from diplomacy, science, faith, culture and innovation to celebrate the Multiverse of Trust, deepen friendships and nurture collaborations in the service of peace and human flourishing.

Inspired by The Post-Quantum Constitution, the evening embraces the vision of a Common House: a future in which different cultures, traditions and disciplines meet through mutual respect, human dignity and shared responsibility. It is an invitation to consider how artificial intelligence, quantum technologies and robotics can support a more humane and peaceful coexistence.

Building on last year’s collaboration, Professor Filippo Gregoretti joins this journey through an artistic encounter connecting music, visual expression and artificial intelligence. His work, and the themes explored in Togetherness, offer a creative reflection on our common purpose: transforming division into dialogue and creating connections through shared experience.

The reception will also feature a book signing of the Italian edition of The Post-Quantum Constitution with its author, Professor Gabriele Pao-Pei Andreoli, offering guests an opportunity for personal exchange on the ideas and responsibilities shaping our technological future.

Looking ahead, the evening will introduce The Spirit of Quantum, the theme of our next chapter, and invite the World Changers community to reunite on 22 October 2027 in Vatican City State.

The evening’s programme

•⁠ ⁠Welcome cocktail and personal encounters.
•⁠ ⁠Reflections on the Multiverse of Trust and the Common House by Professor Andreoli.
•⁠ ⁠Artistic encounter with Professor Filippo Gregoretti.
•⁠ ⁠Book signing of the Italian edition of The Post-Quantum Constitution.
•⁠ ⁠Introduction of The Spirit of Quantum and the 2027 gathering.
•⁠ ⁠A shared toast to peace, friendship and future cooperation.

Together, building trust. Together, nurturing peace. Together, shaping our Common House.

title: Rome hosts the 10th World Changers Summit: art, science, and faith united in “Transcendence”
excerpt: On October 21 and 22, Rome will become the world center for dialogue between ethics, science, and spirituality, hosting the…
html:
On October 21 and 22, Rome will become the world center for dialogue between ethics, science, and spirituality, hosting the tenth edition of the World Changers Summit, organized by the Institute for Advanced Studies and Cooperation (IASC) under the leadership of its president, Professor Gabriele Pao-Pei Andreoli.

The initiative, internationally recognized for its interdisciplinary and humanistic vision, has for years brought together scientists, entrepreneurs, academics, and institutional leaders to address global challenges related to technological evolution and human progress. The summits conceived by Andreoli, who also serves as President of Ethical AI for the Italian League for Human Rights (LIDU Onlus), have become key platforms for promoting ethical innovation and international cooperation.

The 2025 summit, entitled “Transcendence: Unveiling the Future of Humanity ,” will be divided into two distinct moments:

• on October 21st , at the Princess Halls of Palazzo Brancaccio, the last princely residence in the Capital, in a meeting reserved for international guests;

• October 22nd , in the evocative setting of the Pontifical Academy of Sciences in the Vatican. Holy Mass will also be celebrated in the Church of the Artists (Santa Maria in Montesanto), in Piazza del Popolo on October 22nd at 7:00 PM.

“In a world moving at the speed of code,” says Professor Andreoli, “we come together not only to anticipate the future, but to shape it, in a place where innovation meets consciousness, science embraces faith, and humanity imagines its rebirth.” In addition to his academic role, Andreoli also serves as the Vatican Liaison Representative to the Pontifical Academy of Theology and as the Ambassador of the Catholic Church to North Macedonia .

During the two-day event, the Italian premiere of the book “Transcendence: Quantum Computing, AI, and the Future of Humanity,” written by Professor Andreoli and published by La Bussola Edizioni, will be presented. This will consolidate the author’s position as one of Italy’s leading figures in scientific and cultural diplomacy abroad.

A particularly significant moment of the Summit will be the donation by American artist Rob Prior , who has created a work for the occasion dedicated to the message of His Holiness Pope Leo XIV , a symbol of the eternal dialogue between faith, science, and creativity. The painting, which will be presented and blessed in the Vatican, represents a gesture of brotherhood and universal unity, uniting artistic expression with the therapeutic and spiritual value of creation.

The donation will support the research and development program for the treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), promoted by the IASC Longevity Lab in collaboration with the Red Cross of North Macedonia. A project in which art becomes a medicine for the soul and a concrete tool for healing and human cooperation.

Source:https://www.insidemagazine.it/2025/10/15/roma-accoglie-il-10-world-changers-summit-arte-scienza-e-fede-unite-nella-trascendenza/

title: Pastor Dr. Mark Burns Invited to Speak at the Pontifical Academy of Sciences, Vatican City 10th Annual World Changers Summit

Pastor Dr. Mark Burns Invited to Speak at the Pontifical Academy of Sciences, Vatican City 10th Annual World Changers Summit

This distinguished invitation was extended by Sir Prof. Dr. Gabriele Pao-Pei Andreoli, President of the Institute for Advanced Studies and Cooperation, Founder of the World Changers Summit, and Liaison Representative to the Pontifical Academy of Theology – Vatican.

The Pontifical Academy, one of the world’s most respected institutions for dialogue between faith, science, and humanity, gathers global leaders, Nobel laureates, and religious representatives to address issues vital to the moral and spiritual progress of humankind. Its mission-to unite faith and reason in the service of truth and peace-closely aligns with Dr. Burns’ lifelong commitment to promoting interfaith harmony and defending the freedom of belief.

Dr. Burns will be accompanied by the ALLATRA International Public Movement, led by its President Maryna Ovtsynova, whose organization has been instrumental in advancing global humanitarian dialogue and the vision of unity and peace. Ms. Ovtsynova is honored to return to the Vatican – where ALLATRA received Apostolic Blessings from His Holiness Pope Francis in 2024 and His Holiness Pope Leo XIV in 2025 – extending these blessings to the President and all volunteers of the Movement.

Dr. Burns will address the Academy during a special session on interfaith cooperation and the moral responsibility of leadership in the pursuit of global peace. His remarks will emphasize the rising global movement of Spiritual Diplomats, dedicated to building bridges across faiths and nations in defense of human dignity and liberty.

“It is a profound honor to speak at the Vatican’s Pontifical Academy of Sciences,” said Dr. Burns. “At a time when the world faces division and despair, faith must again become the bridge between nations. Peace is not merely the work of governments-it is the sacred duty of all people of conscience.”

This historic invitation reflects international recognition of Pastor Burns’ tireless efforts to promote peace, reconciliation, and freedom through interfaith diplomacy and moral leadership.

title: Maestro Olen Cesari: A Live Neuro-AI Performance Merging Sound, Visuals, and Human Emotion at the World Changers 10th Anniversary Celebration

We are thrilled to present Maestro Olen Cesari, a renowned violinist and composer, at the World Changers 10th Anniversary Celebration. Maestro Cesari is celebrated for his exceptional technique and his ability to seamlessly blend classical and contemporary elements, creating innovative performances that captivate audiences worldwide.

During the performance, the Amrita algorithm will respond to the musical expression of the harmonium, an ancient votive instrument, and Maestro Cesari’s violin improvisations. The result is Transcendence: a living artwork that composes visuals and music from human neural impulses, embodying the tension between an evolving, seemingly “immortal” algorithm and the fragile impermanence of its physical substrate.

Cesari’s virtuosity breathes life into the dialogue with artificial intelligence, blending spontaneity with precision. The performance unfolds as a unique sensory journey, where tradition and innovation converge on stage, inviting the audience into an immersive space where emotion is expressed beyond words.

This collaboration represents the first step of a long-term research trajectory exploring new paradigms of artistic expression in which brain activity, artificial intelligence, and human creativity converge in evolving, co-created works of art. Transcendence challenges us to reflect on the responsible integration of brain data into creative systems and the balance between eternity and transience in AI-driven art.

The exclusive, invitation-only event will take place on October 21, 2025, in the Princess Salons of Palazzo Brancaccio, Rome’s last princely residence, providing a stunning backdrop where history and innovation converge. The event is organized by the Institute for Advanced Studies and Cooperation (IASC) in collaboration with ICB Verse – Kabena Group and the AI Section of the Italian League for Human Rights (LIDU AI).

Prof. Gregoretti, an accomplished artist, composer, and researcher, in collaboration with Brain.Space, has developed an ongoing experimental research project that explores the co-creative dialogue between human performance, algorithmic intelligence, and neuro-feedback.

This groundbreaking performance interprets brain signals captured during various emotional states, such as meditation, anger, and happiness, through Amrita, Gregoretti’s generative Artificial Artistic Evolving Personality. As the brain signals are processed, they transform into evolving artistic expressions, offering a new way of visualizing inner emotions and experiences.

The project is truly at the intersection of technology and creativity, opening new frontiers in how human experience can be expanded and enriched through these two domains. By bridging the gap between technology and artistic expression, Prof. Gregoretti’s work pushes the limits of what is possible in both the artistic and technological realms.

At the World Changers 10th Anniversary Celebration, we will have the privilege of witnessing the first public preview of this live neuro-AI performance. This groundbreaking work exemplifies the power of artificial intelligence and neurotechnology to transform personal emotions into a dynamic and evolving artistic journey.

Through the generosity and vision of internationally renowned artist and World Changer Rob Prior, art becomes a catalyst for healing. His donation supports the IASC organization and World Changers initiatives, especially the IASC Longevity by Design Lab, in collaboration with the Red Cross of Northern Macedonia. This R&D project focuses on children and patients suffering from PTSD, using creativity to directly impact vulnerable lives. Rob’s commitment showcases how art can transcend expression and create tangible change, turning creativity into a force for resilience and hope.

“Transcendence” by Prof. Filippo Gregoretti: The First Public Preview of a Live Neuro-AI Performance
An ongoing experimental research project by Prof. Filippo Gregoretti—artist, composer, and researcher—in collaboration with Brain. Space. This pioneering work explores the co-creative dialogue between human performance, algorithmic intelligence, and neuro-feedback. Brain signals, captured during states of meditation, anger, and happiness, are interpreted by Amrita, Georgetti’s generative Artificial Artistic Evolving Personality. Through this process, inner emotions are transformed into evolving artistic expressions, opening new frontiers in understanding how technology and creativity can merge to expand human experience.

Maestro Olen Cesari: Producing a Dynamic, Interwoven Landscape of Sound and Visuals
During the performance, the Amrita algorithm will respond to the musical expression of the harmonium—an ancient votive instrument—and the exceptional improvisations of renowned violinist Maestro Olen Cesari. The result is Transcendence: a living artwork that composes visual and musical harmony from human neural impulses, embodying the tension between an evolving, seemingly “immortal” algorithm and the fragile impermanence of its physical substrate. Cesari’s mastery brings a human heartbeat to the dialogue with artificial intelligence, blending spontaneity with precision. The encounter unfolds as a unique sensory journey, where tradition and innovation converge on stage.

The audience will be invited into an immersive contemplative space where emotion is expressed beyond words. The interaction of human consciousness, algorithmic intelligence, and sensory experience will give rise to a singular artistic ecosystem. Transcendence represents the first step of a long-term research trajectory, exploring new paradigms of artistic expression in which brain activity, artificial intelligence, and human creativity converge in evolving, co-created works of art.

This collaboration reflects the mission of the IASC World Changers: to convene ethics, science, and culture in service of the human person. By merging space-validated neurotechnology Brain. Space, living AI art Amrita, and human performers, Transcendence opens a space for reflection for scholars, artists, and the public alike on the responsible integration of brain data into creative systems, the co-evolution of human intention and machine adaptation, and the relationship between eternity and transience as an evolving algorithm inhabits impermanent machines—an echo of the book’s central themes.

ICB Verse – Network Gala Dinner
In one of the most beautiful and historic halls of the Brancaccio Palace, the Gala Dinner will celebrate the finest traditions of Italian cuisine while creating a unique space for dialogue, exchange, and connection. More than just a dining experience, it is an opportunity for participants to meet, share perspectives, and build lasting relationships in an atmosphere where culture, history, and innovation come together in harmony.

The World Changers 10th Anniversary Celebration promises to be a transformative and inspiring event, bringing together thought leaders, innovators, and changemakers to explore the future of humanity in an era of rapid technological advancement. Prof. Dr. Gabriele Pao-Pei Andreoli’s Transcendence offers a timely and essential exploration of the intersection between technology, ethics, and human dignity. As we mark a decade of impact, we look forward to continuing to lead the conversation on how technology can be harnessed for the betterment of all humankind.

Prof. Dr. Gabriele Pao-Pei Andreoli is a distinguished academic, humanitarian leader, and researcher with expertise in AI, quantum science, ethics, and international diplomacy. He is the President of the Institute for Advanced Studies and Cooperation (IASC), LIDU Ethical AI, and the World Changers Summit. He is a recognized leader in advocating for responsible AI development and the integration of ethical principles into emerging technologies.

Prof. Andreoli has been honoured with numerous awards, including the Knight of the Order of St. Gregory the Great, “Man of the Year” at the AIMS Conference, and the “Capri Award” for his contributions to blending ethics, science, and faith. Film to serve as catalyst to series of events focused on world peace

VATICAN CITY – ELYSIAN, an international luxury lifestyle brand created to inspire and reflect the interests of women over 35, will host the European premiere of Ukraine: For the Children in Rome, Italy, this month in front of thought leaders, global changemakers and visionaries from around the world.

The premiere will serve as the catalyst to a series of events that ELYSIAN Founder and Publisher Karen Floyd will use to highlight the often-unspoken truth: women have a unique ability to drive meaningful peace efforts, especially when the stakes are high.

“Until the power of love is greater than the love of power, we will not have peace,” she said.

This film is a sequel to ELYSIAN Production’s Fight for Ukraine: 12 Women’s War, a ten-time award-winning, feature-length documentary that was produced in 2023.

The screening of Ukraine: For the Children, on November 25, 2024, will be followed by the reveal of ELYSIAN’s Winter Peace on Earth issue. Guests will then be treated to a visit to the Pontifical Residence at the Vatican followed by a formal gala dinner organized by the Institute for Advance Studies and Cooperation (IASC) to honor ELYSIAN and the remarkable contributions of Floyd and their esteemed guests.

This distinguished gala dinner will inaugurate the World Changers Ethical & Innovation Summit in the historic Hall of the Pontiffs within the Vatican, featuring a tribute performance of “Ave Maria” by Franz Schubert, presented by the renowned violinist Olen Cesari.

On November 26, at the prestigious Pontifical Lateran University, thought leaders, innovators, policymakers, and visionaries from around the globe will gather in the main hall to tackle big issues — artificial intelligence, regenerative medicine, environmental sustainability, and social responsibility — through the lens of ethics and innovation.

Floyd, who launched ELYSIAN nearly 10 years ago in Spartanburg, South Carolina, will open the summit along with IASC President Sir Prof. Gabriele Pao-Pei Andreoli and Prof. Vincenzo Buonomo, Rector of the Pontifical Lateran University. Floyd will then moderate a key panel on social responsibility, specifically as it relates to world peace from a woman’s perspective.

As ELYSIAN approaches its 10th Anniversary in 2025, the brand’s stake in such a prestigious event at the Vatican is emblematic of its journey from a quarterly print publication to today include digital, streaming and exclusive events.

“It is a privilege to both moderate and participate in the World Changers Summit,” Floyd said. “For three reasons: to exchange different perspectives, transcend boundaries, and explore solutions to bold concepts like peace.”

The panel will feature female leaders from different hemispheres, religions and backgrounds: Former Ambassador of India Chitra Narayanan; Fatma Megrahi, who has spent over a decade doing humanitarian work in conflict-affected regions, including Iraq, Ukraine, Somalia, and the Turkish border to Syria; S.C. Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette; Dr. Christina Rahm, a scientist and entrepreneur who is founder and CEO of DRC Ventures; and Anita Winter, a human rights advocate and daughter of Holocaust survivors.

One of the most powerful moments will come with the presentation of a series of vignettes from Ukraine: For the Children. These film clips will spark discussions about the humanitarian role women play in conflict prevention and peacebuilding. Women, especially in times of war, are often the peacemakers and protectors.

Ukraine: For the Children has already amassed three accolades: Best Documentary Feature at the Rome International Movie Awards, Best Documentary Feature at the New York International Film Awards, and Best Documentary at the Eastern Europe Film Festival. It has thus far been selected for numerous other festivals, including the Touchstone Independent Film Festival, the Red Dirt Film Festival, the Life Film Fest – Park City, the Melbourne Lift-Off Film Festival, and the Sydney Lift-Off Film Festival.

Founded in 2022, the summit draws talent and leadership from a variety of sectors, including government, business, academia, and civil society.

ELYSIAN, whose mantra is “Women Inspiring Women,” launched in 2015 and has evolved into a comprehensive multimedia brand. ELYSIAN Impact, the brand’s philanthropic arm, has disbursed more than $16 million over the past eight years to charities in five areas: women, children, animals, service, and the environment.

For more information, visit https://readelysian.com/vatican.

title: Historic Summit at Vatican Sets Stage for Future of Global Innovation and Cooperation
excerpt: As the master of ceremonies at the World Changers Summit, held at the Vatican’s venerable Pontifical Academy of Sciences on…
html:
As the master of ceremonies at the World Changers Summit, held at the Vatican’s venerable Pontifical Academy of Sciences on May 29, 2024, I was privileged to witness a remarkable convergence of global leaders, scientists, entrepreneurs, and thinkers. These visionary figures, united by a shared goal to address critical global issues, gathered to explore innovative solutions. This year’s summit, building on the foundational dialogues from the inaugural event on July 5, 2023, underscored our ongoing commitment to impactful and sustainable global change.

The summit opened with Sir Gabriele Andreoli, founder of the World Changers Summit, whose eloquent remarks set the tone for a day of high-level discussions. He welcomed the diverse assembly to this historic venue, emphasizing the potential for transformative ideas to emerge from their collaboration.

Dr. Christina Rahm was a standout in the morning sessions, exploring how natural remedies can complement modern medical practices in her talk, ‘Our Bodies Remember.’ Her revolutionary work in health and sciences was recognized at the summit with a Red Cross Silver Medal, highlighting her leadership in integrating traditional and contemporary medical approaches.

The mornings agenda also featured Martina Luise, who delved into the “Church and Technology,” and Dario Spera, who introduced cutting-edge developments in “HIT Technology and Regenesis.” Alena Yudina’s session, “The Metaverse for Good,” explored the implications of emerging technologies, contributing depth to the summit’s focus on technology. Additionally, Clayton Thomas, founder of Root Wellness, spoke from the heart, offering a deeply personal perspective on what it means to be a world changer.

Hollywood actor Jordi Molla also captivated the audience with stories of how his faith has profoundly shaped his career and personal life. He eloquently connected his faith-driven decisions to the broader impacts they have on society, offering a rare glimpse into the life of an entertainer who integrates his spiritual beliefs with his professional actions. His account provided attendees with a compelling example of how deeply-held personal beliefs can influence career choices and contribute positively to societal change.

The days leadership discussions were notably enriched by Jessica Word and Robert Grant, who were both knighted at the summit by the Order of Merit of the Portuguese Royal House. Their talks, “Family Values” and “Codex Universalis,” underscored their influential roles as change makers. At the summit, they were also awarded Red Cross Silver Medals in recognition of their efforts to promote ethical leadership grounded in fundamental values and universal truths.

As the day unfolded, Cardinals Peter Turkson and Pietro Parolin addressed the summit, with Cardinal Parolin, the Secretary of State of the Holy See, highlighting the Vatican’s support for the summit and its mission to foster inclusive, impactful initiatives.

Queen Diambi Kabatusuila Tshiyoyo Muata from Congo, representing the Bakwa Luntu tribe of the Central Kasaï region in the historic Kingdom of Luba, delivered a captivating presentation titled “The Beginning” at the summit. Her talk focused on Africa as the cradle of humanity, providing profound insights into the continent’s central role in the global historical narrative. Her presentation not only educated but also inspired attendees to acknowledge and appreciate the profound legacy of Africa in the world’s collective history.

Faith Malton’s speech titled “Being Different” captivated the audience with its heartfelt and powerful message. Born with only one arm, Faith shared how she views her difference not as a limitation but as her superpower. Her ability to intertwine humor with deep emotional resonance made the audience both laugh and cry, drawing them into her experience of turning perceived barriers into strengths. Faith’s message was clear: our differences are what make us unique and can be sources of extraordinary ability, not disability. Her talk not only challenged conventional perceptions of disability but also celebrated the unique qualities that each individual brings to the table.

Kirill Vekhov’s talk on “Unity in Diversity” followed, emphasizing the essential role of diverse perspectives in driving innovation across corporate and societal levels. He shared his personal journey, beginning with his birth in Moscow and his emigration to the USA at the age of 19. While still mastering the English language, he started his first company, highlighting the challenges and triumphs of navigating a new culture and business environment. His compelling presentation underscored how embracing a variety of viewpoints can lead to richer, more creative solutions in both business and community challenges. Kirill also spoke passionately about his efforts to help immigrants, supporting them in their moments of need. He discussed the importance of creating supportive communities that help newcomers integrate and succeed, underscoring the value of diversity and inclusion in building strong, resilient societies.

The summit also featured incredible musical performances by the internationally renowned singers Giuseppe Tedeschi and Maria Ratkova. Their captivating performances left the audience spellbound, earning them enthusiastic applause. The beautiful music added an extra layer of emotion and connection to the event, reminding everyone of the unifying power of the arts. Their talents truly shone through, enriching the summit experience and highlighting the cultural significance of such gatherings.

The summit reached its conclusion with powerful speeches from author Julia Golding and Dr. Keith Dorsey, who each focused on themes that are highly relevant in today’s world. Julia Golding’s presentation, titled “Past, Present, and Future,” explored the continuum of history and its influence on our current strategies and future trajectories. Her speech made a compelling case for using our historical knowledge as a guide in planning and decision-making, emphasizing that learning from the past is crucial for shaping a sustainable future.

Dr. Keith Dorsey’s talk, “Impact Starts with You,” emphasized the significant role of personal initiative in addressing global issues. He argued that the actions of individuals are critical in driving change and that everyone has the capacity to make a difference. In an era where global challenges can seem overwhelming, Dr. Dorsey’s message was a call to action, inspiring attendees to recognize their own power to influence change and to take active steps towards making a positive impact in the world. His speech served as a powerful reminder that change starts on an individual level and that each person’s efforts are vital to collective progress.

As the day’s sessions concluded, Faith Malton, along with other distinguished speakers and organizations such as Dr. Keith Dorsey, Earth05, Reign of Unity, Kirill Vekhov, and Mayor Max Zammit of Ta’ Xbiex, Malta, were honored with awards from the Institute for Advance Studies and Cooperation. This recognition was for their outstanding commitment to excellence, celebrating their significant contributions to their fields and to the summit’s overarching goals of diversity and innovation.

As the summit drew to a close, it became evident that the path to our shared future is shaped not only by the ideas we generate but also by the actions we undertake and the values we embrace. In a world often marked by division, the World Changers Summit served as a powerful reminder that unity creates opportunities— opportunities to innovate, uplift, and transcend.

On May 29, the Vatican’s Casina Pio IV is holding a World Changers Summit, bringing together international representatives of science, technology and faith to discuss the common good.

The World Changers Summit, entitled “Forum to help shape a better future” is now in its third edition. The event was conceived by Professor Gabriele Andreoli, President of the Institute for Advance Studies and Cooperation (IASC).

He has chosen to host the summit at the Pontifical Academy of Sciences, the Vatican venue for dialogue on scientific, theological, technological and moral themes.

Science and technology for the good of people

Andreoli explains: “It’s from the Holy Church that this universal message of hope is being spread to all people based on the concreteness of what we present at this event: a message that sees high science and technology thought out and organized in every detail for the good of people and the world”.

He adds that “there should not and cannot be any distinction, as what drives and guides us is the profound conviction that each human being has their own dignity and should therefore be able to live their life using what science, technology and faith allow us to do today”.

A better future

Achievements that might seem unattainable are instead not only achievable, but realized. And it is at the World Changers Summit that scientific and technological breakthroughs will be shown to shape a better future. Technology, theology, science and faith are at the heart of the World Changers Summit.

Under the banner of the “World Changers Power Women Summit,” Prof. Gabriele Pao-Pei Andreoli, in collaboration with the “Pontifical Academy of Sciences,” orchestrated an evening celebrating the essence of human connection.

The evening resonated with the wonderful concert recital by mezzo-soprano-contralto Countess María Ratkova, accompanied on the piano by pianist Barbara Cattabiani. Beyond the melodies, the room was alive with stories. Dr. Rosario Valastro, National President of the Italian Red Cross, Dr. Domenico Giani, President of the National Confederation of Italian Mercy, and Sister Rosa Opinato were among the esteemed recipients of the 2023 Institute for Advanced Studies and Cooperation Medal of Honor. Their company included luminaries such as Monsignor Dario Edoardo Viganò and H.E. Monsignor Benito Adán Mendez Bracamonte, recognized for their efforts in fostering spiritual unity.

The narrative expanded the next day at the Pontifical Academy of Sciences, Vatican City-State. Voices of female leadership, including Jessica Word, Dr. Christina Rahm, Yulia Stark, Genoveva Turcu, Florina L. Onetiu, Shevon Harris-Holyfield, Dariia Vasylieva, Patrizia Marin, Helene Blanchette, Yasmeen Sehbai., Prof. Maria Garito, Manuela Ronchi, Karen Falkler and Professor Konstantina Papathanasiou shared their insights. The event was truly remarkable, not only for the inspiring women in attendance but also for the invaluable perspectives shared by men who recognized the profound influence of women in their professional and personal lives. Among them were Sir. Robert Grant, Ted Baker, and Marius Marinoff, all eager to recount the profound influence of remarkable woman who have shaped and transformed their personal and professional experiences.

Amidst this backdrop, Jessica Word and Robert Grant received dynastic knighthoods, marking milestones in their distinct journeys.

Dr. Christina Rahm, emblematic of resilience and wisdom, was honored with the Order of Merit Medal by the Portuguese Royal House. Making this day even more historic in Vatican history were the 2023 IASC Medal of Honor recipients: notable figures like Cardinal Peter Turkson, the internationally renowned painter, portraitist, and artist, Count Prof. Giuseppe Tedeschi; Countess Maria Ratkova; and the highly respected Prof. Vittorio Sgarbi.

This was no ordinary event; it was a celebration of human narratives and the connections that enrich our world. With 2023 setting such a compelling stage, anticipation builds for the revelations the 2024 World Changers Summit will bring.

The recent World Changers Summit, held at the prestigious Pontifical Academy of Sciences in Vatican City-State, was a captivating gathering of brilliant minds all dedicated to crafting a brighter future.

Spearheaded by Prof. Gabriele Andreoli, President of the IASC – Institute for Advanced Studies and Cooperation, the event brought together a diverse ensemble of world-changers. The grand inauguration by H. E. Rev. Cardinal Peter K.A. All attendees received an advance copy of Prof. Andreoli’s forthcoming book, “Evolutionary Biohacking”, providing an intellectual keepsake. The Evolutionary Biohacking sessions stood out, featuring Dario Spera’s talk on “Holographic Information Transfer” and Rowena Gates’ insights on body repair—both mind-blowing and revolutionary in scope.
The day culminated with the awards ceremony, where Dr. Christina Rahm was honored with the “Bright Star” award for her contributions to the advancement of medical science.

In the closing session, “Connecting the Dots: Past, Present, and Future”, esteemed speakers like Dr. Lawrence Krauss and Akhtar Badshah delved into the vastness of the universe and the significance of equity in our rapidly evolving world.
Looking ahead, anticipation is building for the groundbreaking World Changers Power Women’s Summit on October 13th. Stay tuned for more exhilarating updates on this must-attend event!

Going onto details about the big day, Prof. Gabriele Andreoli, President of IASC – Institute for Advance Studies and Cooperation, had the vision to put together his best talented friends and inspiring people from different fields and uncommon background with the dream of changing the world, in the best possible way. Prof. Andreoli made it happen in a sunny perfect Roman day and all of us are still so excited for the experience we shared and the first results achieved. A book will be released soon with the best thoughts shared.

The World Changers Summit promises to be a landmark event, bridging the gap between technology, science, and faith, fostering dialogue and collaboration for a better, more understanding world.

title: Meet The Elite and Extraordinary Minds
excerpt: Imagine spending a perfect day filled with captivating presentations by multitudes of experts in their respective fields, in a beautiful…
html:
Imagine spending a perfect day filled with captivating presentations by multitudes of experts in their respective fields, in a beautiful and historic place, and the chance to mingle with each of them on a deeply personal level. That is what The World Changers Summit, held on July 5th at The Vatican and organized by the Institute for Advance Studies and Cooperation (IASC) in partnership with Sir Dustin Plantholt, also known as the Count of Monte Crypto and Sir G.C.H. Prof. Gabriele Andreoli, President of the Institute for Advanced Studies and Cooperation was all about.

Not only was I lucky enough to attend, invited by the illustrious Master of Ceremonies, Sir Plantholt himself, but I also had the privilege of singing for the attendees in the Pontifical Academy of Sciences in Vatican City-State, where the event took place.

To be invited to such a melting pot of minds was a dream come true, especially in such a religious place. Sir Plantholt and Sir Andreoli, Author of newly-released book “Evolutionary Biohacking” — more on that in this article — organized a beautifully-curated stream of aficionados for the day. The event was breathtaking, and I was able to learn from so many masterminds and maestros in their crafts.

Prof. Andreoli said, “Our aim was to unite diverse voices in a shared commitment to creating a brighter future, and we’ve indeed succeeded.”

In this piece, I hope to evoke some sense of the atmosphere awarded to us by their mastery with my humble recap of the event.

Speakers Galore

Sir Plantholt and Sir Andreoli were such gracious hosts for not only myself as the singer, but also to every single attendee. There were multiple authorities in their respective crafts, which was the most interesting part of this function.

The remarkable opening ceremony, led by H. E. Rev. Cardinal Peter K.A. Turkson, established the tone, while Sir Plantholt, the charismatic host, fostered an infectious atmosphere throughout. Reflecting on the experience, Sir Plantholt said, “Facilitating such inspiring conversations among the world’s brightest minds was truly a privilege.”

The event was wonderfully intimate, allowing geniuses in the worlds of science, technology, religion, Web3, blockchain, the metaverse, and more to speak on stage and further mingle with their audience in an efficient and inspiring way. It was like hearing a key chapter from each master’s novel, giving way to riveting discussions during networking pauses throughout the event.

Being invite-only, this manner of facilitating experts in their field sharing with other experts for cross-disciplinary unification made it all the more special.

In short, each person in the room was highly-established and well-known in their field. From Mr. Joe Foster, Founder of Reebok, sharing an unforgettable keynote speech, to Dr. Michael Tjalve, Chief AI Architect of Microsoft Philanthropies, as the first speaker of the day — discussing “The Social Fabric and AI Equity as a Foundational Tenet” — no moment was dull. There were Nobel Peace Prize winners and cardinals, leaders and dignitaries. There were people who had done very great developments in the fields of science, wellness, and physics. The list goes on and on.

Some of my favorite lecturers were Dr. Lawrence Krauss and Akhtar Badshah, wherein “Connecting the Dots: Past, Present, and Future,” they reminded all of us about how small and significant, yet beautifully-advanced our home planet is in which we live.

It was so interesting to be able to hear everyone’s perspectives and hear what they felt was crucial to share during their time on stage. Like a giant TED Talk convention for the ages, the audience members and I were positively inundated with knowledge. Things I’d never thought to consider were brought to my attention, which I will bring into the rest of my year and beyond.

Meet The Founders

Sir Plantholt and Sir Andreoli were such gracious and thought-provoking hosts. In our discussions leading up to the event, it was imperative to them that The World Changers Summit at The Vatican was astounding to all who attended, but, more importantly, the pair expressed ardent wishes for a coming together of great minds, to bring real change into today’s world. On all counts, they did not disappoint.

Sir Plantholt, aptly known as The Count of Monte Crypto, is also the Founder of the Monte Crypto Club, an elite group that includes Nobel Peace Prize winners, renowned crypto experts, and even the Hollywood elite. His moniker, in conjunction with The World Changers Summit, is of course reminiscent of the inspiring story of The Count of Monte Cristo, which revolves around the dissemination of knowledge, empowering individuals to generate wealth, and fostering unity among those who deserve it or are in dire need.

Turning our attention to Sir Andreoli, we are met with another brilliant leader. Adorned with accolades and esteemed recognition, he is something of an icon. His successes include the Red Cross Silver Cross Medals (Italy and San Marino), the United Nations Medal, and the E.U. Medal. However, the most recent and thrilling achievement of Sir Andreoli is the publishing of his new book, “Evolutionary Biohacking”, which details a new way of personal wellness in the wake of the Covid-19 pandemic. The publishing of this fascinating piece of work was unveiled at The World Changers Summit.

“Evolutionary Biohacking is a holistic and powerful way to manage your body, ‘spirit’ and mind, an interesting approach to life, to higher performance, wellbeing and happiness and consciousness expansion, that can give you up to 200% more memory and productivity, 400% more creativity,” he said.

In fact, there was an entire section of the event dedicated to the topic of Evolutionary Biohacking, with Dario Spera’s speech on “Holographic Information Transfer” and Rowena Gates’ discourse on body repair working in perfect harmony to further open our minds to this vital topic. All guests were given an advance copy of Sir Andreoli’s book, a truly momentous and illuminating memento to be cherished.

Everyone who was scheduled to speak had the same opportunity to express themselves in the best way possible, to talk about whatever they wished to talk about for ten minutes straight. Some presenters brought visuals, others had us up on our feet and moving around. Being able to physically see the difference in what each speaker felt was important to bring to their audience was fascinating. Some specialists even did their entire presentations in Italian, which was truly spellbinding and added to the atmospheric charm of the event.

My Time on Stage

I would be remiss if I didn’t chronicle my time on stage. My opening song was Ave Maria, for which I actually received a standing ovation. After my performance, I was told by multiple attendees that being able to hear such a sacred Catholic hymn in such a sacred city, the most religious city in the world, was a blessing and a spiritual moment. I felt the same way.

Singing in the heart of the only city in the Western world where church and state are ruled one in the same, was a truly remarkable and fulfilling experience.

The second song I sang was O Mio Babbino Caro. I chose it because of its Italian heritage, which was a ‘tipping of the hat’ so to speak to the country in which I was performing.

Awards Ceremony

Being invited to this incredible event by such acclaimed people as Sir Plantholt and Sir Andreoli was an immense honor. The hosts even held an awards ceremony, granting prestigious awards to select contributors for their work across different fields. I am honored to have received an award for my contribution to global and societal impact. Of significant note, Dr. Christina Rahm was recognized for her outstanding achievements in advancing medical science and was presented with the prestigious “Bright Star” award.

Changing The World

The overall sense of the event was one of unity and peace. It was one of coming together for the greater good, for sustainability, and for benevolent collaboration. I believe that in The Vatican that day, more harmony between such different spheres of thought and study was born.

The event’s name itself was undoubtedly a perfect selection, and being in that room made it all the more real. I concretely felt that with so many masterminds in one place, we are on the precipice of something actually world-changing. The possibilities seemed endless in such high company.

I am not alone. Many attendees expressed their hope of a repeat event, and we were not disappointed. According to Sir Plantholt’s announcement at the event, The World Changers Power Women’s Summit will be held at The Vatican on October 13th of this year 2023. Since it is invite-only, past attendees anxiously await our invitations, and are on the edge of their seats to find out who will be sharing their grand ideas on stage.

About the World Changer’s Summit

World Changers Summit (WCS) is an event series that brings together individuals from all walks of life to make a positive impact on the world. Since its inception in 2008, WCS has attracted thousands of builders, pioneers, and innovators who are passionate about making a difference. WCS promises to elevate attendees’ spiritual perspectives and empower them to create meaningful change in the world. For more information about upcoming events, please visit https://iascoop.org/

title: Meeting with the Holy Father
excerpt: Meeting with the Holy Father was one of the most incredible experiences, it really gave us the straight to carry…
html: Meeting with the Holy Father was one of the most incredible experiences, it really gave us the straight to carry on and accomplished the first WCS. Pope Francis said “the indisputable benefit that humanity will be able to draw from technological progress depends on the degree to which the new possibilities at our disposal are employed in an ethical manner” He spoke of a “technocratic paradigm” that promises the imposition of uncontrolled and unlimited progress that endangers the whole of humanity. Instead, the Pope encouraged concretely fostering “the culture of encounter and interdisciplinary dialogue”. Pope Francis already had sent a message to the plenary meeting of the Pontifical Academy of Sciences, which is discussing the contribution of science for the survival of humanity. “How wonderful it would be if the growth of scientific and technological innovation could come along with more equality and social inclusion,” the Pope said. “How wonderful would it be, even as we discover faraway planets, to rediscover the needs of the brothers and sisters who orbit around us!”
